key_insight: A frozen general-purpose LLM can propose low-energy quantum circuit parameters for structured Hamiltonians, but performs worse than Adam optimization on general random Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: LLM-generated circuit parameters enable independently verifiable energy estimates, making them more reliable engineering outputs than unvalidated direct energy predictions.
method: Generate complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions.
Evaluate random, structured parent, and molecular Hamiltonians, plus blind circuit interpretation.
evidence_signal: Evaluations found limited gains from iterative feedback, promising low-energy configurations for structured Hamiltonians, and direct energy predictions that could violate spectral lower bounds.
watch_item: Do not treat LLM parameter generation as a general replacement for numerical optimization; independently evaluate every proposed circuit.
paper_title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
